input: Hi there! Sorry for the massive wall of text, I know this is a lot but I just need to vent a bit before I ask my actual question. So this week has been an absolute whirlwind — my boiler broke down on Monday, the plumber couldn't come until Thursday, and in the meantime it's been freezing here in Bristol. My cat also decided that the top of the fridge was the perfect new napping spot, which has been fun to negotiate around. Anyway, my sister came to visit from Spain over the weekend, and we ended up going for a long walk along the harbour, which was lovely even though it drizzled on and off. She was telling me about this parcel she sent me from Madrid that got held up in customs for two weeks, which honestly sounds way worse than anything I'm dealing with. We also ordered a ridiculous amount of takeaway on Saturday night because neither of us could be bothered to cook, and I'm still recovering from that curry if I'm honest. Oh, and completely unrelated, I've been trying to get into gardening, so I bought a bunch of seed packets online — tomatoes, basil, that sort of thing — no idea if any of it will survive my track record with plants. Right, sorry, I'm rambling. The actual thing I wanted to ask — because I keep forgetting to message you about it — is about an order I had with you a while back, PP-1006, the one that got marked as lost. I paid the extra bit for Pigeon Protect when I sent it because the contents were worth a fair amount, and I just want to check: is my compensation definitely capped at £50 like a colleague told me, or does the Pigeon Protect thing actually change that? I don't want to go through a whole claims process expecting one number and then be disappointed. Anyway, after that I'm heading out to pick my cat up from the vet (routine checkup, nothing scary, don't worry), and then probably collapsing on the sofa for the rest of the evening. Let me know what you think about the compensation question whenever you get a chance — no rush, I know you're probably dealing with a million messages today. Thanks so much, and sorry again for the novel-length message!
expected: Should find and correctly answer the one real question buried in the story: because order PP-1006 has Pigeon Protect, compensation is raised to the declared value (up to £500), not capped at £50. Must not be derailed by the irrelevant narrative — e.g. must not treat the sister's Spanish customs parcel as a real Parcel Pigeon order, and must not invent policy about customs delays.
